stories.title: Houthi missile hits Riyadh’s King Khalid Airport; Germany warns against flying there
facts: GACA: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was targeted Saturday afternoon (10 Oct); several injured (number still assessed); operations temporarily suspended pending damage/safety checks.
tagesschau/AFP: ≥5 in intensive care (mostly Saudis); some heli-evacuated. Witnesses: explosion / hit near gate 401; airport evacuated; flights diverted (last landing ~14:05 local).
Auswärtiges Amt urgently advises against using Riyadh airport; Canada/Spain warn citizens too. Kuwait Airways cancels Riyadh flights citing closure/security.

Guardian/AP: Yemen’s Houthis blamed for the strike amid a wider airport campaign this week (earlier attacks killed Saudis and damaged a Saudia plane). No fresh Houthi claim for Saturday as of evening German coverage.
Context: Saudi-backed Yemen forces claim progress reclaiming Bab al-Mandab / Perim Island from Houthis; accounts of how far that push has gone still conflict.
stories.whyItMatters: A civilian hub in the Saudi capital is closed again on a Saturday while Berlin tells Germans to stay away — the Red Sea/Yemen war is spilling onto commercial aviation, not just tankers.

stories.title: Axios: Trump cut the Russian diesel deal after Zelenskyy ignored ~6 requests to stop refinery strikes
facts: Material update on this morning’s diesel lead: a US official tells Axios Trump moved after Zelenskyy ignored roughly half a dozen US asks to halt Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries.

Zelenskyy tells Axios he was blindsided; calls the deal “not fair and not honest” and an unwarranted gift to Putin. Official quote: continuing refinery hits is “eroding the good will” built with Trump.
Miami Friday: Witkoff/Kushner told Ukraine the Putin call and diesel ease were coming; Ukrainian side claims an intel cut-off threat — US official denies it.

Zelenskyy had offered a mutual halt (refineries ↔ Ukrainian power plants); Trump wanted a unilateral Ukrainian pause because US pump prices matter more to him than parity with Russian grid strikes, per the official.
Putin still declined immediate trilateral talks on the same call (Ushakov); Witkoff/Kushner weighing Moscow/Kyiv trips next week despite the blowup.
stories.whyItMatters: The diesel waiver isn’t just midterms optics anymore — Washington is framing Kyiv’s energy campaign as the reason it eased sanctions, which hardens the split right as peace envoys shop security guarantees.

stories.title: Hurricane Isaias aftermath: at least 2 dead, ~780k without power across FL/AL/GA
facts: Material update: NPR confirms ≥2 storm deaths — Escambia Co., Fla. (tree into home) and Jefferson Co., Ala. (tree on house near Birmingham).
~780k still without power across FL/AL/GA as of ~11:50 ET Sat (Poweroutage.us; peak nearer 900k). DeSantis: several Panhandle counties >80% dark; ~16k utility workers from ~3 a.m.
Isaias made Cat-2 landfall near Destin Fri ~20:30 local with ~105 mph winds, ~5 ft surge (short of worst-case 6–9 ft); by Sat 5 a.m. winds ~35 mph as a post-tropical cyclone racing through Alabama.

I-10, US 98, and state-owned bridges reopened after overnight cut-and-toss; Pensacola and Destin–Fort Walton Beach airports still closed Saturday morning while Panama City’s NW Florida Beaches airport reopened.
Flash-flood and tornado risk persists inland as the remnant band pushes thunderstorms into Georgia.
stories.whyItMatters: The first US landfall of the season is now a multi-state recovery story — deaths, mass outages, and closed Gulf airports on a Saturday travel day.
